  <title>Muni Bounds Back in September, Hitting Post-Pandemic Ridership Record</title>
  <link>https://www.sfmta.com/blog/muni-bounds-back-september-hitting-post-pandemic-ridership-record</link>
  <description>  <p>Have some place to be in San Francisco? Muni can get you there. Muni hit a post-pandemic milestone last month, with 555,000 average daily weekday rides, as people flocked to public transit to head to work, school and special events. In all, riders took 15 million Muni trips in September, which translates into 84% of the system’s pre-pandemic ridership. But the story behind the topline number reveals how San Franciscans and visitors rely on Muni. It’s a tale of growth almost across the board, driven in part by our relentless focus on customers and on service that is critical to the city. All of...</p>

  <title>Four Million Trips and Counting: How Bikeshare Moves San Francisco</title>
  <link>https://www.sfmta.com/blog/four-million-trips-and-counting-how-bikeshare-moves-san-francisco</link>
  <description>  <p>San Francisco’s bikeshare network is on track to record 5 million total rides in 2026. San Francisco bikeshare has reached a major milestone. Riders took more than 4 million trips using the Lyft Bike system between January and September 2026. That's more rides than in all of 2025! If current trends continue, we could see more than 5 million bikeshare trips this year. The city's bikeshare network is a vital part of San Francisco's transportation system.   <link>https://www.sfmta.com/blog/your-holiday-wardrobe-muni-style</link>
  <description>  <p>Our 2026 Muni Holiday Sweater is here! And we’ve got sizes available for the whole family. The holidays are right around the corner, and you’ll be able to count on at least two things this year. First, Muni will get you wherever you need to go all season long. And second, you can dress festively to impress with the 2026 Muni Holiday Sweater. The holiday season means something different for everyone.   <link>https://www.sfmta.com/blog/overnight-maintenance-puts-shine-munis-t-third-corridor</link>
  <description>  <p>Muni’s Track Maintenance staff is power washing boarding platforms along the T Third corridor this fall as part of a new overnight maintenance program. While the city sleeps, the streets take on a quiet calmness. Meanwhile, Muni’s Track Maintenance team is wide awake. You may not see them, but their work benefits your ride. Building on the success of Fix It! Weekends this summer, we have developed a proactive maintenance program for the T Third focused on corridor upkeep and reliability.   <link>https://www.sfmta.com/blog/celebrating-our-safe-driver-award-winners</link>
  <description>  <p>Cassandra Griffin, also known as Cable Car Cassandra, is one of our Safe Driver Award winners this year. Being a Muni operator is an important and challenging job. It’s not easy to drive a cable car, streetcar or 40- or 60-foot bus through the streets of San Francisco. Yet, hundreds of operators have stepped up to the plate and get behind the wheel every day. They keep our city moving up and down San Francisco’s iconic hills. They help people get everywhere, including to work, school, the grocery store and the doctor.   <title>Speed Camera Report: 18-Month Study Shows Sustained, Positive Impact</title>
  <link>https://www.sfmta.com/blog/speed-camera-report-18-month-study-shows-sustained-positive-impact</link>
  <description>  <p>The SFMTA released San Francisco’s Speed Study 18-Month Report on Oct. 15, 2026. It’s been 18 months since the SFMTA launched the Speed Safety Camera Program. And our data shows that speeding is down substantially at locations where cameras have been installed. • Excessive speeding is down 84% across camera locations. • That translates to more than 42,000 fewer instances of speeding every day. Our analysis is supported by an independent study by UC Berkeley. Cal researchers also found that the program reduced speeding in San Francisco.   <link>https://www.sfmta.com/blog/working-city-e-device-safety-our-approach-and-tips-stay-safe</link>
  <description>  <p>We're working to help you enjoy the benefits of e-devices while making streets safer for everyone. E-devices are an affordable way to get around, and they quickly have become an important part of our transportation network. E-devices make it easier to get up hills. They help people bridge the “last mile” to transit. And they’re practical for families. But San Francisco has seen a sharp increase in serious injuries involving stand-up electric scooters.
